Splits the free-text guest-list answer into guests (spec section 3, "Splitting the free-text guest list"). The result only pre-fills the sponsor's portal; the sponsor confirms or fixes it. Matching buyers to sponsors and imported guests to guests already on the gala list (spec section 4). Plain rules, first rule that answers wins. Nicknames and typos aren't detected; staff merge by hand.

Normalization for matching only (spec section 4). Never use these for display: names are stored and printed exactly as typed (spec section 3).

The CSV upload path, before the database (spec sections 2–5 and 8): read the export, filter to this gala's page, resolve tiers, split guest lists, match buyers and guests, find missing purchases, and build the report. The result goes to `gl_import()`, which stays the only place that writes. Left to `gl_import()` because they need the stored rows: skipping unchanged rows, `guest_text_changed`, never filling seats a sponsor or staff already named, and the all-or-nothing transaction.
The purchase key: a SHA-256 of the buyer's email and the purchase time, so the CSV upload and the live sync recognize the same purchase.
Reads AAFE's Give Lively ticket export (spec section 1) into validated purchase rows. One row per purchase. Columns are found by header name, ignoring case, spacing, and punctuation.

Reading amounts, counts, and purchase times from the Give Lively export (spec section 1). Each parser returns null for a blank cell and throws ValueError for one it can't read.

AAFE Gala check-in sync server (prototype — synthetic data only). Plain Node http, no dependencies. Persists to sync-server/data.json, first seeded from the door list's check_ins. The iPad check-in app and the staff app both read/write here, so an arrival on the iPad shows up in the staff app. GET /api/health GET /api/checkins?event_id=ev-2027 -> { check_ins, closures, server_time } POST /api/checkins body: CheckIn (id optional) -> { ok, check_in, duplicate } DELETE /api/checkins/:id (undo) -> { ok, removed } POST /api/closures body: { event_id, guest_ids[], closed_by } ("Close gala": remaining guests = no-show) DELETE /api/closures/:event_id (re-open gala) POST /api/reset restore seed…

Build-time guard: secret keys must never reach the browser. Vite copies every VITE_* variable into the built JavaScript, so anyone who opens the app can read it. The Supabase URL and the anon / publishable key are public by design (access rules protect the data); the service_role / secret key bypasses every access rule and must stay in Supabase's Edge Function secrets. This stops the build if a VITE_* variable holds one. See docs/keys-and-secrets.md.

Give Lively donation -> the normalized row gl_import() expects. Give Lively documents the Zapier JSON endpoints but not the field names in each donation object, so fields are found by name, ignoring case, spaces, underscores and nesting ("Transaction ID", "transaction_id", donor.email all match). The names follow the "Line Items (All)" CSV report. Before launch, run one poll against AAFE's account and check givelively_raw: rows marked 'unmapped' mean a name below needs adding. Docs: https://www.givelively.org/resources/understand-zapiers-json-endpoints

Polls Give Lively's Zapier JSON endpoint and imports new gala purchases. Runs every 15 minutes from pg_cron (database/cron.sql); a gala_admin can also trigger it from the staff app ("Pull now"). Secrets: GIVELIVELY_ORG_ID, GIVELIVELY_API_KEY (Nonprofit Admin Portal -> Zapier API key), CRON_SECRET. Which donations are gala sales: the current gala's Give Lively page name (gala_events.givelively_page_name, e.g. "AAFE's 52nd Annual Gala"), set by staff in the staff app. Not set -> the sync does nothing and says so. Demo: GIVELIVELY_BASE_URL points at the givelively-mock function instead of Give Lively.

Sends STAFF-APPROVED emails from email_log through Resend (team hard rule 4: drafts with approved_at null are never sent). Runs every minute from pg_cron (database/cron.sql). Staff can also call it right after an action so the email goes out immediately. Portal links and QR e-tickets: a fresh token is minted for every portal_link or qr_invitation email. Only its SHA-256 hash is stored (email_mark_sent), so earlier links for that order, or codes for that seat, stop working. Secrets: RESEND_API_KEY, EMAIL_FROM (e.g. "AAFE Gala <gala@aafe.org>", domain verified in Resend), GUEST_PORTAL_URL (e.g. https://gala.aafe.org/), CRON_SECRET. Demo: EMAIL_REDIRECT_TO=<team inbox> sends every email there…

Real-data guard (hard rule 1: no real donor data, ever). Fails if a tracked file contains 1. an email address outside the reserved demo domains (example.org/.com/.net and their subdomains, .test, .example, .invalid) or the short list of public addresses below; 2. a US phone number outside the fictional range 555-0100 to 555-0199; 3. a spreadsheet, or a CSV outside seed/ and fixtures/ (the same rule as .gitignore, which `git add -f` can bypass). It can't recognize a real name, so it's a backstop for reviewers, not a replacement. Run from anywhere in the repo: node scripts/check-no-real-data.mjs
